title: Japchae
subtitle: Korean glass noodles stir-fried with beef and vegetables
excerpt: Japchae is a Korean celebration dish of chewy sweet potato glass noodles tossed with separately cooked beef and vegetables. Each component is cooked on its own for the best colour and texture, then combined. The result is a dish with many flavours in every mouthful.
sourceNotes: Japchae was first made in the seventeenth century for King Gwanghaegun of Joseon. It originally contained no noodles -- they were added later when glass noodles became available. Today japchae is a fixture of Korean celebrations, holidays, and family gatherings. The glass noodles are made from sweet potato starch.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Individual components can be cooked up to 2 hours ahead and kept at room temperature. Toss everything together just before serving.

content.text: Japchae takes patience because each component is cooked on its own before everything is combined at the end. This keeps the colours bright and the textures distinct. Set up a large bowl to collect everything as it comes out of the pan -- the final toss is quick once all the parts are ready.

items.prepNote: blanched for 30 seconds, squeezed dry, and roughly chopped
soaked in hot water for 20 minutes, drained, and sliced
use 200g sweet potato glass noodles (dangmyeon) -- cook per packet, rinse, and cut with scissors
use toasted sesame oil -- for finishing

content.text: Cook the glass noodles according to the packet, drain, and rinse with cold water. Cut with scissors into shorter lengths. Toss with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce.
Season the beef mince with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and a pinch of sugar. Stir-fry in 1 tablespoon of oil over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked. Set aside.
Fry the carrot in 1 teaspoon of oil for 2 minutes. Season with salt. Set aside.
Fry the mushrooms and spring onion in 1 teaspoon of oil for 2 minutes. Set aside.
Add the wilted spinach to the bowl of noodles. Add all the cooked vegetables and beef.
Add the remaining soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, and black pepper. Toss everything together gently. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.cause: Not enough oil or tossed while too dry
items.fix: Toss the noodles with a little oil and a splash of soy sauce immediately after draining. If they stick badly, rinse with warm water, drain again, and toss with the dressing straight away.

content.text: Japchae is a dish for celebrations in Korea. It is served at birthdays, weddings, and Chuseok (harvest festival). The glass noodles have a distinctive chewiness that is different from any other noodle. Cooking each component separately is the key to the dish looking and tasting its best.
